description.zh: 磁场力总垂直于速度，只改方向不改大小，所以带电粒子被弯成圆周运动；转一圈的时间与速度无关，只由电荷、质量和磁场定——质谱仪正是按这个周期（实际按半径）把不同质量的粒子分开，速度选择器则只放行特定速度的粒子。经典、单粒子、教学单位。
description.en: A magnetic force is always perpendicular to velocity, so it changes direction but not speed, bending a charged particle into a circle. The time per lap does not depend on speed, only on charge, mass and field — a mass spectrometer separates particles by this period (in practice by radius), and a velocity selector passes only one speed. Classical, single particle, teaching units.

label.en: The cross product gives the force direction

reason.zh: 磁力方向既不沿 v 也不沿 B，而是同时垂直于两者——没有矢量叉乘就说不清这个方向，右手定则就是它的操作版。
reason.en: The magnetic force points neither along v nor along B, but perpendicular to both — without the vector cross product there is no way to state that direction, and the right-hand rule is its working version.

label.zh: 圆周运动的投影是振动
label.en: A circle projects to an oscillation

reason.zh: 粒子绕圆匀速运动，其一个坐标随时间按正弦变化，周期与速度无关。
reason.en: Uniform motion on a circle makes each coordinate vary sinusoidally, with a period independent of speed.

reason.zh: 第 4 步让电力 qE 与磁力 qvB 方向相反，平衡时 v = E/B。
reason.en: Step 4 sets the electric force qE against the magnetic force qvB; they balance at v = E/B.

title.en: How does a magnetic field make a particle circle?

ask.zh: 带电粒子在磁场中受力，力的方向和速度、磁场各是什么关系？
ask.en: A charged particle in a magnetic field feels a force — how does its direction relate to the velocity and the field?

ask.zh: 力总垂直于速度——速度大小变吗？只改变方向的力会让粒子走什么轨迹？
ask.en: The force is always perpendicular to the velocity — does the speed change? What path does a force that only changes direction produce?

ask.zh: 粒子转圈的周期和速度有关吗？质谱仪怎样利用这一点区分粒子？
ask.en: Does the circling period depend on speed? How does a mass spectrometer use that to tell particles apart?

reveal.zh: 磁场力总垂直于速度，只改方向不改大小，粒子就做圆周运动；周期与速度无关，质谱仪按周期（实际按半径）区分不同质量。
reveal.en: The magnetic force stays perpendicular to velocity, changing direction but not speed, so the particle circles; the period is speed-independent, and a mass spectrometer separates masses by the resulting radius.
